description: [interpret] Sandboxed Evaluation — replace Phase 1's isolated-context + materialization with in-place compilation into the caller's heap, add a map-based capability prelude resolved at compile time, and downgrade non-core builtins to env lookups in sandbox mode so the prelude actually controls capability. Closure-return support is punted.

userStories.title: source_to_closure_in_place compile helper
userStories.description: As the VM, I want a helper that lex/parse/macro-expands/compiles a source string into a JaclClosure on a caller-supplied heap, so that [interpret] can produce a runnable closure without spinning up a new jacl_context_t.
acceptanceCriteria: New function in src/vm.c (or near compiler driver) with signature roughly: JaclVal source_to_closure_in_place(const char *src, size_t len, arena_t *arena, ThreadHeap *heap, JaclInternTable *intern_table, ExpandState *expand, JaclError *err_out) — returns a closure value or JACL_NIL with err_out populated
Internally calls lexer_lex → parser_parse → compiler_compile using the supplied arena/heap/intern_table/expand; does NOT create a jacl_context_t
Produced closure's bytecode and captured state live on the supplied heap (parent GC sees them via normal root scanning)
Parse errors populate err_out->kind = JACL_ERROR_COMPILE with the first AST_ERROR message
Compile errors populate err_out->kind = JACL_ERROR_COMPILE with cr.error_message
On error, no partial state leaks into caller's heap/intern table beyond what normal compilation would (arena-scoped)
Integration test: valid source compiles to a closure, calling it produces expected value
Integration test: parse error returns JACL_ERROR_COMPILE with message
Integration test: compile error returns JACL_ERROR_COMPILE with message

userStories.title: Rewrite OP_INTERPRET using in-place compile
userStories.description: As the maintainer, I want OP_INTERPRET to use source_to_closure_in_place and call the resulting closure on the parent VM, so that we can delete the isolated-context, result-materialization, and complex-value-rejection code.

userStories.title: Compiler accepts prelude map as compile-time env seed
userStories.description: As the compiler, I want to accept an optional JACL map whose keys populate the compile-time environment before I walk the AST, so that interpreted code resolves names against caller-supplied capabilities instead of the accumulated-from-source env.

Reserved keys (e.g. :core) are NOT registered as names — documented as reserved for future config flags; default is core-always-on

Unresolved name references produce compile errors via existing error path (cr.error_count > 0, message like "undefined name 'foo'")

userStories.title: [interpret-prelude] builtin returns default permissive prelude
userStories.description: As a caller of [interpret], I want a builtin that returns the default permissive prelude map (including interpret itself), so that I can derive restricted preludes by removing keys with map-remove rather than enumerating every capability.
acceptanceCriteria: New opcode-based builtin [interpret-prelude] (0 args) in src/compiler.c — compiles to a new OP_INTERPRET_PRELUDE opcode

VM handler constructs a map containing an entry for every non-core builtin name recognized by the compiler, with values being native-fn references or sentinel callables that route to the opcode

userStories.title: Non-core builtin opcode-vs-env downgrade in sandbox mode
userStories.description: As the compiler, when compiling under a caller-supplied prelude, I want to downgrade non-core builtin references from direct opcode emission to env lookups, so that the prelude map actually controls whether print, spawn, etc. are callable.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler gains a sandbox-mode flag, set when prelude_map is non-nil in compiler_compile

In sandbox mode, when compiling a command whose head is a non-core builtin name: check name against prelude map keys (compile-time); if present, emit OP_GET_GLOBAL/env lookup + OP_CALL against the map entry's value; if absent, emit compile error "undefined name 'foo'"
In sandbox mode, core builtins (arithmetic, comparison, control flow, binding, destructuring, immutable data ops) emit normal opcodes regardless of prelude contents
In non-sandbox mode (no prelude supplied): existing behavior unchanged (all recognized builtins emit their opcodes)
Core vs non-core list captured in single helper bool compiler__is_core_builtin(const char *name, uint32_t len) for auditability
Integration test: [interpret {"print": $my-print} "[print \"hi\"]"] calls $my-print instead of built-in print opcode
Integration test: [interpret {} "[spawn { 42 }]"] is a compile error (spawn not in prelude)
Integration test: [interpret {} "[+ 1 [* 2 3]]"] returns 7 (core arithmetic always works)
Integration test: macro defined inside interpreted code that references a non-core builtin gets the sandbox treatment (macro-expanded output goes through sandbox compile)
